profile.objective: Assess the funding needed to sustain operations and the conditions under which a DCF can inform the decision.
profile.model_rationale: The fictional business sells a subscription for a finance workflow. Recurring revenue and customer churn drive commercial repeatability.
profile.scope: Synthetic SaaS diligence case. Financial amounts are in base USD and the financing rounds are conditional.

documents.name: Opening ownership and proposed financing terms
documents.reviewed: Fully diluted share register and terms

evidence.title: Reported accounts and recurring-revenue ledger
evidence.extract: Fictional historical evidence. Revenue 100000, COGS 40000. At cutoff unrestricted cash 100, net monthly burn 10, excess cash 15, debt 40 and other bridge adjustments -5. Contracted recurring MRR 10. Opening 10 and churned 2 November customers.

evidence.title: Synthetic independent terminal-state and market-rate review
evidence.extract: Fictional benchmark for repeatable subscription economics, stable final-year reinvestment, 12% cost of equity, 5% debt cost, 25% target debt weight, 20% marginal tax, 2% long-run growth and sensitivity inputs.

evidence.title: Operating and capital plan
evidence.extract: Assumed monthly EBIT of 8 / 18 / 23 in downside / base / upside, cash tax 3, D&A 2, capex 5, increase in working capital 2, other net cash flow -15, cash floor 40.

evidence.title: Opening ownership and proposed financing terms
evidence.extract: At cutoff founder 80 shares, option pool 20, two future investors each hold zero. Proposed 15 March 2027 financing 250 pre-money, 25-share pool top-up, angel subscribes 50. Proposed 15 December 2027 financing 450 pre-money, zero top-up, founder and fund each subscribe 30.

evidence.title: Harbour Ledger public offer sheet (synthetic)
evidence.extract: Fictional company offer sheet. Product sold to small finance teams. Entry price stated as USD 40 a month.

evidence.title: Small-business subscription comparison (synthetic)
evidence.extract: Fictional comparison. Harbour Ledger entry listed at USD 55 a month with unclear inclusions. Maple Relay lists USD 35 a month and targets bookkeeping practices.

claims.statement: The reported year ended 30 November 2026 had USD 100,000 of recognised revenue.
claims.rationale: Company-origin ledger. The assessment has no independent reconciliation.

claims.statement: The entry subscription is USD 40 a month for small finance teams.
claims.rationale: The comparison survey shows a different entry price for a plan whose inclusions are unclear.

thesis.management: Subscriptions from small finance teams can support a repeatable model.
thesis.independent: Subscription cash flows can be modelled, but the customer economics and the financing plan need independent validation.
falsifiers: Verified cash shortfall or inability to sustain gross margin

divergences.finding: The fictional website and comparison survey give different entry prices.
divergences.impact: Withhold a like-for-like price comparison for Harbour Ledger until the pricing tiers are reconciled.

factors.question: Resolve legal identity, jurisdiction, ownership and instruments; distinguish operating entity from brand.
Test urgency, alternatives, willingness to pay and demonstrated adoption.
factors.finding: A finance-team offer exists in the fixture. No customer adoption is corroborated.
factors.impact: Demand and willingness to pay remain uncertain.
factors.next_test: Review paid contracts and retained cohorts.

factors.question: Assess current readiness, delivery evidence, differentiation and critical dependencies.
Verify relevant track record, responsibilities, key-person dependency, conflicts and governance.
factors.finding: Management roles and prior execution are unverified.
factors.impact: Execution and governance remain open diligence areas.
factors.next_test: Review roles and prior operating results.

factors.question: Test reachable market, competitors, substitutes, channels and pricing; distinguish top-down TAM from addressable sales.
factors.finding: The sample offers establish some overlap in customer focus. Entry prices require a comparable tier.
factors.impact: The independent price comparison remains incomplete.
factors.next_test: Obtain the dated offer and tier schedule.

factors.question: Reconcile actual revenue and cost structure, monetisation, contribution and repeatability.
factors.finding: Synthetic company statement only; no independent verification.

factors.question: Test cash availability, financing, burn, debt, working capital, runway and future funding needs.
Test durability of differentiation, switching costs, IP rights, scale effects and replication risks.
Identify material licensing, compliance, operational, security and concentration dependencies.
Identify evidence that would invalidate the thesis; determine valuation eligibility and key drivers.
Contracted recurring revenue versus bookings and one-off services; ARR bridge.
factors.finding: The source lists contracted recurring MRR for the cutoff.
factors.impact: Annualised recurring revenue can be calculated from the reported ledger.
factors.next_test: Reconcile contracted subscriptions to billed invoices and credits.

factors.question: Cohorts, GRR/NRR, churn, CAC and payback with consistent definitions.
Hosting and service costs, contribution, support and enterprise sales cycle.

research.reason: Synthetic fixture; no live research performed.

inputs.label: Debt share of market capital value

challenges.finding: No independent verification of cash or commercial thesis.
Reported entry price differs from the comparison survey.
challenges.correction: Show both source references and withhold the comparable entry price.

gaps.why: Cash and runway are not independently verified.

gaps.action: Reconcile comparable entity, date and enterprise value to recognised revenue.

gaps.item: Dated Harbour Ledger offer and contract schedule
gaps.why: The public and independent sample records disagree.
gaps.conclusion: Starting price comparability, commercial positioning and subscription economics.
gaps.action: Reconcile tier inclusions and quote effective dates before updating the comparison.

decision.conclusion: Request funding and cash evidence before deciding. The reported inputs support arithmetic checks and the financing forecast still depends on a proposed close.
decision.limitations: Fictional evidence, parties and figures used to test the reporting contract.
strengths: The input ledger makes the recurring revenue and gross margin calculations reproducible.
risks: The base case still breaches its cash floor after the first conditional round.
The enterprise value is sensitive to the assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

cap_table.rationale: Fully diluted common-equivalent model for two conditional primary closings.

scenarios.rationale: Consistent monthly operating and financing cash flows.

downside.rationale: Weaker trading with neither conditional equity round included.

base.rationale: Steady trading with the first conditional round included.

upside.rationale: Stronger trading with both conditional rounds included.

dcf.rationale: Synthetic established subscriptions and steady-state reinvestment support perpetuity.

competitor_comparisons.title: Finance workflow alternatives
competitor_comparisons.scope: Fictional cloud subscriptions in the US. As of 30 November 2026.

criteria.label: Target customer
criteria.definition: Buyer segment named in the current product offer.

subject.rationale: Public offer sheet states the segment.

maple.rationale: The comparison survey identifies the intended customer.

criteria.label: Starting monthly price
criteria.definition: USD per account per month, before sales taxes, for the entry-level offer.

subject.rationale: The sources give different entry points and plan inclusions need reconciliation.

maple.rationale: Price and unit are stated in the comparison survey.
